title: Shepherd's Potato
rawIngredients: 2 tbsp olive oil, plus a little bit extra
3 sprigs fresh rosemary, plus extra to serve
120g cooked puy lentils (home-made or from a packet)
method: Preheat the oven to 200°C[cite: 2]. Prick the baking potatoes with a fork, rub with 2 tablespoons olive oil, salt, and pepper, and bake on a tray for 45–60 minutes until soft[cite: 2].
Finely chop the white onion, celery, and carrot[cite: 2]. Finely chop the chestnut mushrooms[cite: 2].
Heat a splash of oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat; sauté the chopped onions, celery, and carrots for 5–10 minutes until starting to soften[cite: 2].
Crush the garlic into the pan[cite: 2]. Strip the leaves from the rosemary and thyme stems, finely chop them, and add to the pan[cite: 2]. Season and cook for 2–3 minutes[cite: 2].

Add wholegrain mustard, tomato purée, and soy sauce, then reduce heat to a light simmer[cite: 2]. Stir in the finely chopped mushrooms and cooked lentils; cook for 5–7 minutes[cite: 2]. Pour in the vegetable stock and mix[cite: 2].

Remove potatoes from the oven and let cool slightly[cite: 2]. Cut a round lid off the top of each potato, scoop out the fluffy centers leaving at least a 1cm lining, and mash in a bowl with dairy-free butter, nutritional yeast, salt, and pepper[cite: 2].
Fill potato skins to the brim with mushroom mince and top with a dollop of mashed potato[cite: 2]. Bake in the oven for 10–15 minutes until crispy[cite: 2].
Sprinkle each potato with chilli flakes, remaining chopped rosemary, and black pepper before serving[cite: 2].
